title: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out
body:
Read the chapter → [Leviticus 6](/bible/leviticus/6)

## Introduction

This reading covers [Leviticus 6](/bible/leviticus/6) through 9: the trespass offering and restitution, the laws of the burnt, meat, sin, trespass, and peace offerings, the consecration of Aaron and his sons, and the eighth day when the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people. Leviticus is straightforward like the rest of the law, and these chapters pertain heavily to the book of Hebrews: the law of sacrifice is the volume of the book that is written of Christ, and once you understand the law you begin to understand the letters of Paul. The session opened by backtracking into [Leviticus 5](/bible/leviticus/5) on the witness law, unclean things, and oaths; that teaching belongs to the [Leviticus 5](/bible/leviticus/5) chapter set and is logged there.

**[Leviticus 6:1-5](/bible/leviticus/6#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/6#v1)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/6#v2)</sup> If a soul sin, and commit a trespass against the Lord, and lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or in a thing taken away by violence, or hath deceived his neighbour;
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/6#v3)</sup> Or have found that which was lost, and lieth concerning it, and sweareth falsely; in any of all these that a man doeth, sinning therein:
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/6#v4)</sup> Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away, or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten, or that which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found,
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/6#v5)</sup> Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering.

- If a soul lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or deceive his neighbour, or find that which was lost and lie concerning it, and swear falsely, the Lord counts all of it as a thing taken away by violence: verse 4 says he shall restore that which he took violently away. Deceiving your neighbour, going into agreement and not holding up your end, or lying about what was given you to hold is a violent act toward your neighbour, and a Ponzi scheme or pyramid scheme sits right in that law.
- He shall restore it in the principal: the value of what was taken had to be given back, with more added on top. A sorry would not settle it with the Lord; you could end up in debt for years over sticky fingers.
- Stealing was not a sin unto death, but the Lord made the restitution heavy so you would never commit it again. It goes back to the commandment, thou shalt not steal, and to the civil law where an ox was restored fivefold and a sheep fourfold.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 20:15](/bible/exodus/20#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/20#v15)</sup> Thou shalt not steal.

    Thou shalt not steal; the trespass law enforces this commandment.
  - **[Exodus 22:1](/bible/exodus/22#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/22#v1)</sup> If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

    Five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep; the thief restored the principal many times over.

**[Leviticus 6:6-7](/bible/leviticus/6#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/leviticus/6#v6)</sup> And he shall bring his trespass offering unto the Lord, a ram without blemish out of the flock, with thy estimation, for a trespass offering, unto the priest:
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/leviticus/6#v7)</sup> And the priest shall make an atonement for him before the Lord: and it shall be forgiven him for any thing of all that he hath done in trespassing therein.

- The trespass offering was a ram without blemish, perfect as the Most High made it, and the priest made an atonement for him before the Lord and it was forgiven him. The sacrifice stood in your place for your sin.
- The whole law of sacrifice points to Christ, who came in the volume of the book. He is the offering without blemish and the atonement, and who has become the high priest is Jesus the Christ.
- Israel became the enemy of the Most High by sin. There are two kinds of enemies: the nations that are the natural enemies of the Most High, and Israel, who rebelled and vexed his holy spirit, and he was turned to be their enemy. Through the death of his Son the nation is reconciled, brought back together with its God.
- The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 10:7](/bible/hebrews/10#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/hebrews/10#v7)</sup> Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.

    Lo, I come in the volume of the book it is written of me; the whole book from Genesis to Revelation points to Christ.
  - **[Isaiah 63:7-10](/bible/isaiah/63#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/isaiah/63#v7)</sup> I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/isaiah/63#v8)</sup> For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/isaiah/63#v9)</sup> In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/isaiah/63#v10)</sup> But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.

    The great goodness toward the house of Israel; but they rebelled, and he was turned to be their enemy.
  - **[Romans 5:10-11](/bible/romans/5#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/romans/5#v10)</sup> For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/romans/5#v11)</sup> And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

    When we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, by whom we have now received the atonement.
  - **[Ezekiel 45:17](/bible/ezekiel/45#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/ezekiel/45#v17)</sup> And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.

    The sin offering, meat offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel; that is what reconciled means.
  - **[Acts 5:30-31](/bible/acts/5#v30)**
    > <sup>[30](/bible/acts/5#v30)</sup> The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.
    >
    > <sup>[31](/bible/acts/5#v31)</sup> Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.

    Him hath God exalted to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins; Christ died for the nation of Israel.

**[Leviticus 6:8-9](/bible/leviticus/6#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/leviticus/6#v8)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/leviticus/6#v9)</sup> Command Aaron and his sons, saying, This is the law of the burnt offering: It is the burnt offering, because of the burning upon the altar all night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar shall be burning in it.

- The burnt offering burned upon the altar all night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar was burning in it. When Exodus says kindle no fire on the sabbath day, that speaks of making food; the Levites were commanded to keep a fire burning on the altar continually, sabbath included.
- Christ used this very law on the Pharisees: have ye not read how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? The priests had fire going in the temple every sabbath by commandment.
- I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: the Most High desired the knowledge of God and obedience more than burnt offerings. Israel leaned so heavily on the sacrifices instead of applying the commandments that they were confounded and could not see Christ as the Son of God when he came.
- Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 35:3](/bible/exodus/35#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/35#v3)</sup> Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.

    Kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day; that is fire for cooking, not the altar fire.
  - **[Matthew 12:5-7](/bible/matthew/12#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/matthew/12#v5)</sup> Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/matthew/12#v6)</sup> But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/matthew/12#v7)</sup> But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.

    On the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless; if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
  - **[Hosea 6:6](/bible/hosea/6#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/hosea/6#v6)</sup> For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

    For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
  - **[Malachi 2:7](/bible/malachi/2#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/malachi/2#v7)</sup> For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.

    The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth; the knowledge the Most High desired is the law.
  - **[Jeremiah 7:21-23](/bible/jeremiah/7#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/7#v21)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/7#v22)</sup> For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices:
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/jeremiah/7#v23)</sup> But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.

    Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded obedience: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.

**[Leviticus 6:10-11](/bible/leviticus/6#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/leviticus/6#v10)</sup> And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and his linen breeches shall he put upon his flesh, and take up the ashes which the fire hath consumed with the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/leviticus/6#v11)</sup> And he shall put off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry forth the ashes without the camp unto a clean place.

- The priest put on his linen garment and his linen breeches upon his flesh. The priests were men, not women, and breeches are pants; they were made for the men.
- The ashes of the burnt offering were carried forth without the camp unto a clean place. Christ fulfilled that figure: they led him away out of the city to crucify him at Golgotha, the place of a skull; he suffered without the gate.
- Hebrews draws the lesson: let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. Put away the sacrifice as it was carried outside the temple, and come out unto Christ.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 28:42](/bible/exodus/28#v42)**
    > <sup>[42](/bible/exodus/28#v42)</sup> And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover their nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:

    Linen breeches to cover their nakedness were made for Aaron and his sons; the breeches belonged to the men.
  - **[Matthew 27:31-33](/bible/matthew/27#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/matthew/27#v31)</sup> And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him.
    >
    > <sup>[32](/bible/matthew/27#v32)</sup> And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to bear his cross.
    >
    > <sup>[33](/bible/matthew/27#v33)</sup> And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,

    They led him away to crucify him, and came unto a place called Golgotha; led away is the same as carried without the camp.
  - **[Hebrews 13:10-14](/bible/hebrews/13#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/hebrews/13#v10)</sup> We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/hebrews/13#v11)</sup> For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/hebrews/13#v12)</sup> Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/hebrews/13#v13)</sup> Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/hebrews/13#v14)</sup> For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.

    The bodies of the beasts are burned without the camp; wherefore Jesus also suffered without the gate; let us go forth unto him without the camp.

**[Leviticus 6:12-13](/bible/leviticus/6#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/leviticus/6#v12)</sup> And the fire upon the altar shall be burning in it; it shall not be put out: and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and lay the burnt offering in order upon it; and he shall burn thereon the fat of the peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/leviticus/6#v13)</sup> The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out.

- The fire upon the altar shall be burning in it; it shall not be put out. The priest burnt wood on it every morning, and that included the sabbath; the fire shall ever be burning upon the altar, and it shall never go out.
- This is exactly what Christ went into in Matthew 12: the priests profane the sabbath and are blameless, because the commanded altar fire never went out.

**[Leviticus 6:14-18](/bible/leviticus/6#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/leviticus/6#v14)</sup> And this is the law of the meat offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before the Lord, before the altar.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/6#v15)</sup> And he shall take of it his handful, of the flour of the meat offering, and of the oil thereof, and all the frankincense which is upon the meat offering, and shall burn it upon the altar for a sweet savour, even the memorial of it, unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/leviticus/6#v16)</sup> And the remainder thereof shall Aaron and his sons eat: with unleavened bread shall it be eaten in the holy place; in the court of the tabernacle of the congregation they shall eat it.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/6#v17)</sup> It shall not be baken with leaven. I have given it unto them for their portion of my offerings made by fire; it is most holy, as is the sin offering, and as the trespass offering.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/leviticus/6#v18)</sup> All the males among the children of Aaron shall eat of it. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations concerning the offerings of the Lord made by fire: every one that toucheth them shall be holy.

- This is the law of the meat offering. The meat offering is not flesh; it is grain, fine flour with oil and frankincense. A handful was burnt upon the altar for a sweet savour, and the remainder Aaron and his sons ate unleavened in the holy place.
- It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: the law is spiritual. To understand how a perpetual statute of sacrifice pointed to Christ, the Spirit of Christ had to dwell in you; Paul himself did not understand until Christ touched him on the way to Damascus.
- Christ told the disciples the Comforter would teach them all things and bring all things to their remembrance. Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws; that is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees, for the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

  Precepts:
  - **[Romans 7:14](/bible/romans/7#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/romans/7#v14)</sup> For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

    For we know that the law is spiritual; the statute for ever is understood in the spirit.
  - **[John 14:26](/bible/john/14#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/john/14#v26)</sup> But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.

    The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance; the spirit of the law is revealed by the Spirit.

**[Leviticus 6:19-23](/bible/leviticus/6#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/leviticus/6#v19)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/leviticus/6#v20)</sup> This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons, which they shall offer unto the Lord in the day when he is anointed; the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meat offering perpetual, half of it in the morning, and half thereof at night.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/leviticus/6#v21)</sup> In a pan it shall be made with oil; and when it is baken, thou shalt bring it in: and the baken pieces of the meat offering shalt thou offer for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/leviticus/6#v22)</sup> And the priest of his sons that is anointed in his stead shall offer it: it is a statute for ever unto the Lord; it shall be wholly burnt.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/leviticus/6#v23)</sup> For every meat offering for the priest shall be wholly burnt: it shall not be eaten.

- This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meat offering perpetual, half in the morning and half at night, baked with oil in a pan. The meat offering is again actual flour, grain.
- Every meat offering for the priest was wholly burnt; it was not eaten. The priest's own offering went completely to the Lord.

**[Leviticus 6:24-30](/bible/leviticus/6#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/leviticus/6#v24)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/leviticus/6#v25)</sup> Speak unto Aaron and to his sons, saying, This is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the Lord: it is most holy.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/leviticus/6#v26)</sup> The priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it: in the holy place shall it be eaten, in the court of the tabernacle of the congregation.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/leviticus/6#v27)</sup> Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof shall be holy: and when there is sprinkled of the blood thereof upon any garment, thou shalt wash that whereon it was sprinkled in the holy place.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/leviticus/6#v28)</sup> But the earthen vessel wherein it is sodden shall be broken: and if it be sodden in a brasen pot, it shall be both scoured, and rinsed in water.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/leviticus/6#v29)</sup> All the males among the priests shall eat thereof: it is most holy.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/leviticus/6#v30)</sup> And no sin offering, whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle of the congregation to reconcile withal in the holy place, shall be eaten: it shall be burnt in the fire.

- This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the LORD; it is most holy. Christ was the sin offering, and he was most holy.
- Christ did no sin, neither was guile, which is deceit, found in his mouth; when he was reviled, he reviled not again. He kept his Father's commandments and abode in his love, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps; if you do not keep the commandments of God you are not following his steps.
- The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Peter 2:21-23](/bible/1-peter/2#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/1-peter/2#v21)</sup> For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/1-peter/2#v22)</sup> Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/1-peter/2#v23)</sup> Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously:

    Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.
  - **[John 15:10](/bible/john/15#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/john/15#v10)</sup> If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.

    If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments; that is how Christ walked.
